ARGUMENT

OPEH IS ENTITLED TO
A MONEY JUDGMENT AGAINST DEFENDANTS

CPLR §3213 authorizes a motion for summary judgment in lieu of complaint, providing,
in relevant part, that:

When an action is based upon an instrument for the payment of money only or

upon any judgment, the plaintiff may serve with the summons a notice of motion

for summary judgment and the supporting papers in lieu of a complaint. The

summons served with such motion papers shall require the defendant to submit

answering papers on the motion within the time provided in the notice of motion.

It is well settled that a “plaintiff would prove a prima facie case by proof of the note and
a failure to make the payments called for by its terms.” Seaman-Andwall Corp. v. Wright Mach.
Corp., 31 A.D.2d136, 295 N.Y.S.2d 752 (1968); and, that the threshold requirement for such
prima facie case is the existence of a “’commercial paper in which the party to be charged has
formally acknowledged the indebtedness.’” Weissman v. Sinorm Deli, Inc., 88 N.Y.2d 437, 444,
646 N.Y.S.2d 301, quoting, Interman Indus. Products, Ltd. V. R.S.M. Electron Power, Inc., 37
N.Y.2d 151, 154-155, 371 N.Y.S.2d 675.

Here, OPEH’s motion is based upon Defendants’ failure to make payments pursuant to
the Promissory Note in which, the Defendants formally and explicitly acknowledged their
indebtedness to OPEH. See, Sosnick Aff. at §3. A copy of the Promissory Note is annexed to
the Sosnick Aff. as Exhibit A.

The Promissory Note sets forth payment terms, to wit, Defendants agreed that, for value

received, to pay OPEH the principal sum $2,233,007, with interest at the rate of 10%, per

annum, compounded annually, on or before September 17, 2018. See, Sosnick Aff. at 493 and 5;
